I read p. 34, Lemma A.1 (p. 126) and Lemma A.2 (p. 127), and the Lean sources. Assertion (ii) is formalized closely and in places more strongly: Data (L16) is the printed hypothesis, inverseNorm/quadraticNorm/debtNorm are exactly ν_k, q_k, ‖d‖_{C^k} for the CK norm max_{n≤k} sup_I‖∂ⁿf‖, Small k is the printed threshold, and exists_smooth_same_branch and linear_solution give both of its sentences. Only the family clause fails the logic-alone test: Lean's Family lives on an open parameter set, the paper's lives on a compact one, and no declaration bounds the jets of B⁻¹ over a non-open parameter set. That is a real, if inconsequential, restriction, so DELTA with a low finding.

findings.summary: The family clause of assertion (i) is stated only for data satisfying every hypothesis on an open parameter set U ⊇ K. The paper's family is smooth on the compact parameter set and need not extend; no declaration bounds the jets of B⁻¹ over a non-open parameter set.
No single declaration states Lemma 4.7. Its clauses are four declarations in three files: the matrix invertibility, the family bound, the quadratic solve on [-1,1], and the Q = 0 case.
